questions.prompt: Write the energy equation including nonconservative work.
A friction force of \(6\,\mathrm{N}\) acts over \(4\,\mathrm{m}\) opposite the motion. Find its work.
If \(W_{nc}<0\), what happens to mechanical energy?

questions.answer: Its work depends on path length, not only on starting and ending positions.

questions.prompt: A \(2\,\mathrm{kg}\) block moving at \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) stops due to friction. Find the work done by friction.
A system has \(K_i+U_i=80\,\mathrm{J}\). Nonconservative work is \(-15\,\mathrm{J}\). Find final mechanical energy.
A block slides \(10\,\mathrm{m}\) with \(f_k=3\,\mathrm{N}\). It starts with \(50\,\mathrm{J}\) of kinetic energy. Find final kinetic energy on level ground.
A motor does \(120\,\mathrm{J}\) of work while friction does \(-35\,\mathrm{J}\). Find the net nonconservative work.
A \(1.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) block slides down a vertical drop of \(2.0\,\mathrm{m}\) and friction does \(-6\,\mathrm{J}\). Starting from rest, find the speed at the bottom.
A \(3\,\mathrm{kg}\) block starts at \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and moves up a rough ramp gaining \(1.0\,\mathrm{m}\) of height. Friction does \(-10\,\mathrm{J}\). Find its final speed.
questions.answer:
\[
K_i+W_{nc}=K_f+\Delta U_g
\]
\[
\frac{1}{2}(3)(4^2)-10=K_f+3(9.8)(1)
\]
\[
24-10=K_f+29.4
\]
The right side would require negative \(K_f\), so the block stops before reaching that height.

questions.prompt: A block of mass \(m\) starts from rest at height \(h\), slides down a rough track of length \(L\) with constant friction magnitude \(f_k\), then compresses a horizontal spring of constant \(k\) on a rough floor where the same friction magnitude acts. Derive the maximum compression \(x\) and the condition for compression to be possible.
questions.answer:
The nonconservative work includes friction on the track and friction during spring compression:
\[
W_{nc}=-f_kL-f_kx
\]
At maximum compression, \(K_f=0\). The energy equation is
\[
mgh-f_kL-f_kx=\frac{1}{2}kx^2
\]
Rearrange:
\[
\frac{1}{2}kx^2+f_kx+f_kL-mgh=0
\]
Compression is possible only if the block reaches the spring with positive mechanical energy:
\[
mgh>f_kL
\]
The positive compression is
\[
x=\frac{-f_k+\sqrt{f_k^2+2k(mgh-f_kL)}}{k}
\]
The other quadratic root is negative and is rejected because \(x\) is a compression distance.

questions.prompt: A block starts with speed \(v_0\) and must reach a point height \(h\) above its start. It can take rough path \(1\) of length \(L_1\) or rough path \(2\) of length \(L_2\), with the same constant friction magnitude \(f_k\) on either path. Derive \(v_f^2(L)\), then classify when neither path works, only the shorter path works, or both paths work.
questions.answer:
For a path of length \(L\),
\[
\frac{1}{2}mv_0^2-f_kL=\frac{1}{2}mv_f^2+mgh
\]
Therefore
\[
v_f^2(L)=v_0^2-2gh-\frac{2f_kL}{m}
\]
A path works only if \(v_f^2(L)\geq0\), so
\[
v_0^2\geq 2gh+\frac{2f_kL}{m}
\]
Let
\[
L_s=\min(L_1,L_2),\qquad L_\ell=\max(L_1,L_2)
\]
The regimes are
\[
v_0^2<2gh+\frac{2f_kL_s}{m}:\quad \text{neither path works}
\]
\[
2gh+\frac{2f_kL_s}{m}\leq v_0^2<2gh+\frac{2f_kL_\ell}{m}:\quad \text{only the shorter path works}
\]
\[
v_0^2\geq 2gh+\frac{2f_kL_\ell}{m}:\quad \text{both paths work}
\]
The endpoint height is the same, but friction depends on path length, so mechanical energy loss is path-dependent.
